o: The five-year term of a municipality
The manner of electing the municipal Chairperson
Ward Committees in municipalities with a population of three lakh or more
State Election Commission supervision of municipal elections
82.x: The manner of electing the Chairperson or Mayor is left to the State legislature. The other three are compulsory constitutional provisions.
82.tq: Use the compulsory-versus-voluntary table to identify the discretionary provision.
xs: **The manner of electing the municipal Chairperson** is left to the state — option **(2)**.
The **5-year term**, **Ward Committees** (**3 lakh+**) and **SEC** supervision are compulsory.
xa: AP Cabinet (**18 Aug 2026**) approved **direct election of Mayors** and chairpersons, replacing the indirect system.
Other voluntary items: **BC reservation**, **MP/MLA representation**.

82.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about reservation for women in local bodies?
o: Article 243D deals with reservation in Panchayats.
Article 243T deals with reservation in Municipalities.
The minimum reservation for women is less than one-third of total seats.
Reservation for women also applies to chairpersons' posts.
82.x: At least one-third of seats and chairpersons' posts must be reserved for women under Articles 243D and 243T.
n: Article 243D deals with reservations in Panchayats. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Article 243T deals with reservations in Municipalities. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Reservation for women must be not less than one-third of the total seats. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Reservation for women must be not less than one-third of the chairperson positions. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
One-third reservation is at least 33 percent. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
xa: Composition: **243C** / **243R**, regulated by the **State Legislature**; minimum age **21** years.
**243G / 243W**: economic development, social justice, sanitation, public health.
**243J / 243Z**: audit laws by the **State Legislature**.
**243K / 243ZA**: State Election Commission — superintendence, direction and conduct of local elections.

82.s: Which one of the following is NOT a compulsory provision under the 74th Amendment?
o: Reservation for backward classes in every municipality
Ward Committees in municipalities having a population of three lakh or more
Reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in proportion to population
82.x: Reservation for backward classes is voluntary and is left to the State legislature. Ward Committees for municipalities with a population of three lakh or more, five-year terms, and SC/ST reservation are compulsory provisions.
82.tq: Find the provision expressly left to State legislative discretion among otherwise mandatory features.
xs: **Reservation for backward classes** is **voluntary** — option **(1)**.
Compulsory: **Ward Committees** (**3 lakh or more**), **SC/ST reservation** by population, **5-year** term.
xa: Other voluntary items: representation of **MPs, MLAs, MLCs**; manner of electing the **Chairperson**.
Devolving the Twelfth Schedule subjects (**243W**) is also voluntary.

82.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about municipal tenure and elections?
o: An election must be held within one year of the dissolution of a municipality
A municipality has a five-year term
The State Election Commission conducts municipal elections
The State Finance Commission reviews the financial position of municipalities
82.x: An election must be held within six months of dissolution, not one year.
xa: ⚠ **243K / 243ZA** = SEC; **243I / 243Y** = SFC — one body each for panchayats and municipalities.
The term runs from the **first meeting**.

82.s: Under Article 243U, the five-year term of a municipality is counted from the date of which event?
82.x: A municipality continues for five years from the date appointed for its first meeting, unless dissolved earlier according to law.
82.tq: Distinguish the constitutional starting point from election and notification dates.
xs: The term runs **five years** from the **first meeting** — option **(3)** (**243U**).
Not from the election result, budget session or Governor's notification.
xa: After dissolution, polls within **six months**.
The municipality is **heard** before dissolution.
Panchayat term is also **5 years** (**243E**).

82.s: Under Article 243U, what must a municipality be given before it is dissolved?
o: A reasonable opportunity of being heard
Approval of the State Election Commission
82.x: Article 243U requires that a municipality be given a reasonable opportunity of being heard before its dissolution.
xa: Fresh polls within **six months** of dissolution.
Polls are run by the **SEC** (**243ZA**).

82.s: Under Article 243R, which persons may be represented in a municipality but without the right to vote in its meetings?
o: Officials of the State Election Commission
Persons with special knowledge or experience in municipal administration
Members of the State Finance Commission
82.x: State law may provide for representation of persons with special knowledge or experience in municipal administration, but they cannot vote in municipal meetings.
xa: State law may add **Lok Sabha/Assembly** members for the area.
**Rajya Sabha/Council** members **registered as electors** there may be added.

82.s: What is the fixed term of a Panchayat or Municipality under the 73rd and 74th Amendments?
82.x: Local bodies have a five-year term; after early dissolution elections are held within six months unless less than six months remain.
n: The fixed term of Panchayats and Municipalities is five years. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
If a Panchayat or Municipality is dissolved prematurely, elections must be held within six months. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Elections within six months are not required when the remaining term is less than six months. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]

82.s: Under Article 243V, with reference to what are disqualifications for membership of a municipality mainly determined?
o: Only rules framed by the Union Government
The law made by the municipal council itself
Only the Representation of the People Act, 1951
The law applicable to elections to the State Legislature or a State law
82.x: A person may be disqualified under the law applicable to elections to the State Legislature or under a law made by the State Legislature.
82.tq: Identify the correct level of law governing disqualification.
xs: Disqualifications follow **the law for State Legislature elections or a State law** — option **(4)** (**243V**).
Not Union rules, nor the municipal council's own law.
xa: Minimum age: **21 years**.
Same pattern as panchayats under **243F**.

82.s: Under Article 243R, how are the members of a municipality chosen?
o: Election by MLAs of the area
82.x: Article 243R requires members to be directly elected from wards; State law may add non-voting experts and legislators.

82.s: Municipal Corporations, Municipal Councils and Nagar Panchayats are three types of ___ local Governments.
82.src: AP Grama Ward Sachivalayam Ward Welfare & Development Secret
82.x: Municipal Corporations, Municipal Councils and Nagar Panchayats are the three types of municipalities under Art. 243Q – urban local governments; rural bodies are Panchayats.

82.s:
In the following questions, there are two statements. One is labelled as
Assertion (A) and other is labelled as
Reason (R) :
Assertion (A) : Municipal corporations are formed in big cities having a definite area and population.
Reason (R) : Urban administrations of big cities are very complex in nature. In the context of the above two statements which of the following is correct?
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
82.x: Both are true and R explains A: Municipal Corporations are constituted for larger urban areas (243Q) because the administration of big cities is complex.

82.s: If there is dispute between Panchayat and Cantonment Board, who will decide finally?
o: Collector, subject to approval of Divisional
Divisional Commissioner, subject to approval of
Panchayat and Rural Development Department subject
State Government, subject to approval of Central
82.x: Under s.79(2) of the Chhattisgarh Municipalities Act, 1961, a dispute between a Panchayat and a Cantonment Board is decided by the State Government, subject to the Central Government's approval (cantonments are Central).

82.s: In an area in transition from a rural area to an urban area ______ may be constituted in every State
82.x: Art. 243Q: a Nagar Panchayat is constituted for a transitional area – one in transition from rural to urban; a Municipal Council is for a smaller urban area.

82.s: Under the 74th Amendment, which body is constituted for a smaller urban area?
82.x: Municipal Councils serve smaller urban areas and Municipal Corporations larger ones; Nagar Panchayats are for transitional areas.
n: The institution for a smaller urban area under the 74th Amendment is the Municipal Council. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
The institution for a larger urban area under the 74th Amendment is the Municipal Corporation. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
The 73rd and 74th Amendment systems are interlinked with district planning bodies. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]

82.s: Cantonment Boards come under which Union Ministry?
o: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
82.x: Cantonment Boards are under the Ministry of Defence; MoHUA is the main ministry for ULBs, and Home Affairs handles ULBs in UTs.
xa: ULBs in AP come under the **MA&UD** department.
MoHUA is the **main** ministry; Defence handles only **cantonment boards**.

82.s: Which urban local body falls outside the three types of municipalities recognised under Article 243Q?
82.x: Article 243Q recognises Nagar Panchayats, Municipal Councils and Municipal Corporations; Cantonment Boards lie outside this classification.

82.s: A Municipal Corporation generally comprises which three principal authorities?
o: Mayor, State Finance Commission and Commissioner
Council, District Collector and Standing Committee
82.x: The three principal authorities of a Municipal Corporation are the Council headed by the Mayor, the Standing Committees and the Commissioner.
82.tq: Match the institutional structure rather than individual office-holders.
xs: A Municipal Corporation has a **Council** (headed by the Mayor), **Standing Committees** and a **Commissioner** — option **(2)**.
The **Governor**, the **SFC** and the **District Collector** are not corporation authorities.
xa: The **Municipal Commissioner** (IAS, appointed by the State) is the chief executive.
The **Mayor** (assisted by a Deputy Mayor) presides over the Council.

82.s: As what may the Governor specify an area under Article 243Q where an industrial establishment provides municipal services?
82.x: Under the proviso to Article 243Q the Governor may specify such an area as an industrial township, and a municipality need not be constituted there.
xa: The Governor specifies area types by **public notification**.
Criteria: population, density, revenue, non-agricultural employment, economic importance.

82.s: Which of the following is among the eight types of urban local bodies listed for India?
82.x: The eight types are Municipal Corporation, Municipality, Notified Area Committee, Town Area Committee, Cantonment Board, Township, Port Trust and Special Purpose Agency.

82.s: Under the proviso to Article 243Q, no municipality need be constituted in an area where municipal services are provided by whom?
82.x: Where an industrial establishment provides municipal services, the area may be an industrial township without a municipality.

82.s: Who specifies the areas for Nagar Panchayats, Municipal Councils and Municipal Corporations?
82.x: Under Article 243Q the Governor specifies the areas by public notification on population, density, revenue and similar factors.

82.s: For which kind of area is a Municipal Corporation constituted under Article 243Q?
82.x: Article 243Q gives a Nagar Panchayat for a transitional area, a Municipal Council for a smaller urban area and a Municipal Corporation for a larger urban area.

82.s: Which Act replaced the Cantonments Act, 1924 for the governance of cantonment boards?
82.x: Cantonment boards, under the Ministry of Defence, were governed by the 1924 Act, replaced by the Cantonments Act, 2006.

82.s: Which Union Ministry is the main ministry for urban local bodies in India?
o: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
82.x: MoHUA is the main ministry for ULBs; Home Affairs handles ULBs in Union Territories and Defence handles Cantonment Boards.

82.s: Who is the chief executive of a Municipal Corporation and is ordinarily appointed by the State Government?
82.x: The Municipal Commissioner is the chief executive of a Municipal Corporation and is appointed by the State Government, commonly from the IAS.
82.tq: Apply the “who would do this job?” method to separate political leadership from administration.
xs: The **Municipal Commissioner** (IAS, appointed by the State) is the chief executive — option **(3)**.
The **Mayor** presides over the Council; the **Chairperson** heads a Municipal Council / Nagar Panchayat.
xa: **GVMC** has **zonal commissioners** under the Municipal Commissioner.
Corporation = **Council** + **Standing Committees** + **Commissioner**.

82.s: How many subjects the Twelfth schedule of the Indian constitution contain on which the municipalities are given administrative control?
82.x: The Twelfth Schedule (74th Amendment, Art. 243W) lists 18 functional items of municipalities; the Eleventh has 29.

82.s: Municipalities have Constitutional respon sibilities in respect of which of the following as per the Twelfth Schedule?
82.x: 'Cattle pounds; prevention of cruelty to animals' is item 15 of the Twelfth Schedule; non-conventional energy, small-scale industries and technical/vocational education are Eleventh Schedule (Panchayat) items.

82.s: Which one of the following functions is not the concern of Local Self Government?
82.x: Public health, sanitation and public utility services are local-government functions (Eleventh/Twelfth Schedules); maintenance of public order is State police work, not a local-body function.

82.s: Twelfth Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains ____ functional items.
82.x: The Twelfth Schedule (74th Amendment) lists 18 functional items of municipalities.

82.s: How many functional subjects are listed in the Twelfth Schedule?
82.x: The Twelfth Schedule lists 18 subjects for municipalities; the Eleventh lists 29 for Panchayats.
n: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act concerns rural local self-government. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act concerns urban local self-government. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act contains the 11th Schedule. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
The 11th Schedule contains 29 functional subjects. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act contains the 12th Schedule. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
The 12th Schedule contains 18 functional subjects. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
xa: The 11th Schedule came by the **73rd Amendment, 1992**; the 12th by the **74th Amendment, 1992**.
**9th Schedule** — **1st Amendment, 1951** (land reforms); **10th Schedule** — **52nd Amendment, 1985** (Anti-Defection).
**Part IV-A** (Fundamental Duties, **Article 51A**) — **42nd Amendment, 1976**.
**Part IX-B** (Co-operative Societies) — **97th Amendment, 2011**.

82.s: Which of the following is NOT a Twelfth Schedule subject?
o: Street lighting, parking, bus stops and public conveniences
82.x: Technical and vocational education is an Eleventh Schedule subject; the other three are Twelfth Schedule municipal subjects.
xa: Twelfth also covers **burial and cremation grounds**, electric crematoria.
And **water supply** (domestic, industrial, commercial), **roads and bridges**.

82.s: Which one of the following is NOT a subject in the Twelfth Schedule?
o: Regulation of slaughter houses and tanneries
82.x: Libraries and markets and fairs are listed under the Eleventh Schedule, not the Twelfth Schedule. Urban poverty alleviation, urban forestry and environmental protection, and regulation of slaughter houses and tanneries are Twelfth Schedule subjects.
82.tq: Use the municipal-versus-Panchayat list distinction to identify the excluded subject.
xs: **Libraries and markets and fairs** are **Eleventh** Schedule (panchayat) items — option **(1)**.
**Urban poverty alleviation**, **urban forestry and environment** and **slaughter houses and tanneries** are Twelfth Schedule items.
xa: Other Eleventh-only items: **PDS**, **small-scale industries**, **non-conventional energy**.
Twelfth also has **public health, sanitation, solid waste management**.

82.s:
Assertion (A): The Twelfth Schedule includes functions relating to urban poverty alleviation.
Reason (R): The Twelfth Schedule is concerned exclusively with physical infrastructure such as roads, bridges and water supply.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
82.x: The Assertion is true because urban poverty alleviation is a Twelfth Schedule subject. The Reason is false because the Schedule also covers social, environmental, cultural and regulatory functions, not exclusively physical infrastructure.
82.tq: Test the absolute word “exclusively” in the Reason against the wider range of municipal functions.
xs: **A is true but R is false** — option **(3)**.
A true: **urban poverty alleviation** is a **Twelfth Schedule** item.
R false: the Schedule also covers **welfare**, **health and environment**, **culture** and civic items — not only roads, bridges and water supply.
xa: Welfare items: **weaker sections** incl. disabled; **slum improvement and upgradation**.
Civic items: **vital statistics**, **cattle pounds**, **slaughter houses and tanneries**.
The Twelfth Schedule has **18** items, linked to **Art. 243W**.

82.s: Which of the following is found only in the Eleventh Schedule and not in the Twelfth?
82.x: Technical and vocational education is an Eleventh Schedule item; the other three are Twelfth Schedule items.

82.s: Which of the following is a Twelfth Schedule item absent from the Eleventh Schedule?
82.x: Vital statistics is only in the Twelfth Schedule; non-conventional energy, PDS and libraries are Eleventh Schedule items.

82.s: Ward committees must be constituted in the Municipalities having a population of
82.x: Art. 243S: a Wards Committee is constituted in every municipality with a population of three lakh or more; 10 lakh is the metropolitan-area figure.

82.s: What is correct about the wards committee of Nagar Panchayat? i. Wards committee is formed with some wards of nagar Panchayat. ii. Councillor elected from the wards become its member. iii. Two persons are nominated in the committee residing in the ward. iv. Chairman of the wards committee is nominated by the President of nagar Panchayat.
82.x: Under the Chhattisgarh law the Nagar Panchayat wards committee is formed of some wards, its elected ward councillors are members and two ward residents are nominated; the chairman is not nominated by the President – i, ii, iii (CGPSC key). Art. 243S itself leaves composition to State law.

82.s: Each Ward Committee of a Municipality represents a population of
82.x: Art. 243S: Wards Committees are constituted in municipalities with a population of three lakh or more.

82.s: Under the Community Participation Law, who are the members of an Area Sabha?
o: All elected councillors of the municipality
Members of the Wards Committee only
All voters in a polling-booth area
Members of Parliament from the urban area
82.x: An Area Sabha consists of all voters in a polling-booth area and sits below the Wards Committee.
xa: The **Community Participation Law** was a **JNNURM** mandatory reform.
Wards Committees: **243S**, mandatory at **3 lakh+**.

82.s: Who determines the composition and territorial area of a Wards Committee?
82.x: Under Article 243S, State law determines the composition and territorial area of Wards Committees, which may cover one or more wards.

82.s: The Community Participation Law was identified as a mandatory reform under which programme?
82.x: The Community Participation Law was a mandatory reform under the Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM).
82.tq: Match the reform with the programme under which it was made mandatory.
xs: The **Community Participation Law** was a **JNNURM** mandatory reform — option **(3)**.
The notes link the law only to **JNNURM**, not to the other schemes listed.
xa: It provides for **Area Sabhas** below Wards Committees.
Model Nagara Raj Bill: **2008**.

82.s: In which of the following was the Area Sabha, made up of all voters of a polling-booth area, proposed?
82.x: The Area Sabha comes from the Model Nagara Raj Bill (2008); the Community Participation Law was a JNNURM reform.

82.s: Wards Committees must be constituted in municipalities having a population of at least how much?
82.x: Article 243S makes Wards Committees compulsory in municipalities with a population of three lakh or more.

82.s: DIGIT e-Governance platform, which is currently operational in Andhra Pradesh is associated with which department of the Government of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Department of Information and Public Relations
82.x: AP's urban local bodies run on the DIGIT e-Governance platform of the Municipal Administration and Urban Development (MA&UD) department.

82.s:
Match list-I (Functionaries) with list-II (Institution) and select the correct answer using the codes given below lists.
List-I (Functionaries):

A. Sarpanch

B. Chairperson

C. Mayor

D. Councillor
List-II (Institution):

1. Municipal Corporation

5. Ward
82.x: Sarpanch heads a Village Panchayat, a Chairperson a Municipality, a Mayor a Municipal Corporation, and a Councillor represents a ward: A-2, B-3, C-1, D-5.

82.s:
The State Government controls over urban local bodies:
(A) in legislative matters
(B) in financial matters
(C) in personnel matters
(D) in respect of citizens' grievances
Select the correct answer from the codes given below–
82.x: The State Government controls ULBs in legislative, financial and personnel matters (A, B, C); citizens' grievances are not a head of State control.

82.s: What have critics of urban governance called Urban Local Bodies in Indian federalism?
82.x: ULBs, which spend less than 1 per cent of GDP and employ about 10 per cent of the public workforce, have been called the 'stepchild' of federalism.
xa: **Property tax** is the key own revenue but is chronically **under-collected**.
Cities house **~36%** of India's population.

82.s: Which one of the following is identified as the key own-source revenue of Urban Local Bodies but is chronically under-collected?
82.x: Property tax is the key own-source revenue of Urban Local Bodies, but it is chronically under-collected.
82.tq: Identify the principal own-revenue source rather than a shared tax.
xs: **Property tax** is the ULBs' key own revenue, chronically under-collected — option **(2)**.
The notes name no other tax (stamp duty, motor vehicle or entertainment) as the ULBs' key own revenue.
xa: ULBs spend **less than 1%** of GDP.
Their taxing powers and grants (**243X**) are left to state legislatures.
They are the "**stepchild**" of federalism.

82.s: As per the AP Socio-Economic Survey 2025-26, how many of the State's 123 urban local bodies are Municipal Corporations?
82.x: The Survey 2025-26 lists 17 Municipal Corporations, 76 Municipalities and 30 Nagar Panchayats among AP's 123 ULBs.

82.s: How much reservation for Backward Classes in Andhra Pradesh Urban Local Bodies was provided under G.O. Rt. No. 1065 dated 19 August 2026?
82.x: G.O. Rt. No. 1065 provides 33.33 percent reservation for Backward Classes in Urban Local Bodies.
82.tq: Distinguish the urban reservation figure from the rural reservation figure.
xs: **G.O. Rt. No. 1065** gives **33.33 percent** BC reservation in AP ULBs — option **(2)**.
**34%** is the figure for **rural** bodies.
xa: It is implemented under both municipal laws.
Approved by the AP Cabinet on **18 Aug 2026**.

82.s: Which is the nodal department for Urban Local Bodies in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Municipal Administration and Urban Development Department
Panchayat Raj and Rural Development Department
82.x: The Municipal Administration and Urban Development (MA&UD) Department is the nodal department for ULBs in AP.
xa: Laws: **AP Municipalities Act, 1965** + corporations law.
AP has **123** ULBs.

82.s: Which pair of laws governs municipalities and municipal corporations in Andhra Pradesh respectively?
o: AP Municipalities Act, 1994 and AP Municipal Corporations Act, 1965
AP Municipal Corporations Act, 1956 and AP Municipalities Act, 2001
AP Municipalities Act, 1965 and AP Municipal Corporations Act, 1994
Andhra Pradesh Panchayats Act, 1965 and AP Municipalities Act, 1994
82.x: Municipalities and Nagar Panchayats in AP are governed by the AP Municipalities Act, 1965, and Municipal Corporations by the AP Municipal Corporations Act, 1994. Options A and B swap or misdate the two Acts, and D names a Panchayats Act.
82.tq: Distinguish the two enactments by both subject and year.

82.s: Who is the State Election Commissioner of Andhra Pradesh who notified ward-wise photo electoral rolls for 41 urban local bodies in 2026?
82.x: Anil Chandra Punetha is the AP State Election Commissioner who notified ward-wise photo rolls for 41 ULBs (12 corporations and 29 municipalities/nagar panchayats). The other names are not the current SEC.
xs: AP SEC **Anil Chandra Punetha** notified ward-wise photo rolls for **41 ULBs** — option **(2)**.
These cover **12** Corporations + **29** municipalities/NPs.
xa: Corporations include **GVMC**, **Vijayawada**, **Guntur**, **Tirupati**, **Kurnool**.
Rolls due **22 Sep 2026**; qualifying date **1 Jan 2026**.

82.s: In August 2026, the AP Cabinet approved which method for choosing Mayors and municipal or Nagar Panchayat chairpersons?
82.x: The Cabinet approved direct election of Mayors and municipal or Nagar Panchayat chairpersons, replacing the indirect system.
xa: Under the 74th, the manner of electing the chairperson is **left to the state**.

82.s: Which of the following pairs of functionary and institution is correctly matched?
82.x: The Pradhan heads the Panchayat Samiti; the Sarpanch heads the Gram Panchayat and the Mayor the Municipal Corporation.

82.s: Of which body is the Sarpanch the head?
82.x: The Sarpanch heads the Gram Panchayat; the Pradhan heads the Panchayat Samiti.

82.s: VMRDA was formed in 2018 by dissolving which body?
82.x: VMRDA (G.O.Ms. 302, 5 September 2018) replaced VUDA (1978); it covers Visakhapatnam, Vizianagaram and Anakapalli.

82.s: APCRDA, set up in December 2014, plans and develops the capital region and which city?
82.x: APCRDA under the APCRDA Act (11 of 2014) plans and develops the capital region and Amaravati.

82.s: The AP Municipal Corporations Act, 1994 applies which parent law?
82.x: The AP Municipal Corporations Act, 1994 applies the Hyderabad Municipal Corporations Act, 1955; municipalities come under the AP Municipalities Act, 1965.

82.s: How many Municipalities does Andhra Pradesh have as per the AP Socio-Economic Survey 2025-26?
82.x: AP has 123 ULBs: 17 Municipal Corporations, 76 Municipalities and 30 Nagar Panchayats.

82.s: Which of the following Articles states that seats shall be reserved for the Scheduled Castes in every Municipality?
82.src: General Overview of the Indian Constitution & Welfare Paper-
82.x: Art. 243T reserves seats for SCs and STs (and women) in every municipality; 243S is Wards Committees, 243Q types, 243P definitions.

82.s: Which of the following Articles states that seats shall be reserved for the Scheduled Tribes in every Municipality?
82.src: General Overview of the Indian Constitution & Welfare Paper-
82.x: Art. 243T reserves seats for STs (and SCs and women) in every municipality; 243R is composition, 243S Wards Committees, 243Q types.

82.s: Audit of municipal accounts is provided under which Article?
82.x: Audit of municipal accounts is under Article 243Z; 243X concerns taxes and funds, 243U duration and 243R composition.

82.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding the accounts and audit of Panchayats?
o: The audit arrangement is dealt with under Article 243J.
The State Legislature provides for maintenance of Panchayat accounts.
Panchayat audit laws are enacted by the Union Parliament.
The State Legislature provides for audit of Panchayat accounts.
82.x: Option C is incorrect: under Article 243J, the State Legislature, not Parliament, provides for keeping and auditing Panchayat accounts.
82.tq: Recall who makes the laws on Panchayat audit.
n: Article 243J deals with accounts and audit of Panchayats. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
The State Legislature provides for the maintenance of accounts. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
The State Legislature provides for the audit of accounts. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Panchayat audit laws are enacted by the State Legislature. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Panchayat audit laws are not enacted by the Union Parliament. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
xs: The **incorrect** statement is option **(3)**: Panchayat audit laws are **not** enacted by the **Union Parliament**.

xa: The municipal counterpart of 243J is **Article 243Z**.
Other pairs: **243C / 243R** composition; **243D / 243T** reservation; **243E / 243U** tenure.
**243-I / 243-Y** State Finance Commission; **243K / 243ZA** State Election Commission.

82.s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for Ward Committees?
82.x: Article 243S provides for Ward Committees; 243Q covers types of municipalities, 243R their composition and 243T reservation.

83.s: Who notifies the Scheduled Tribes for a State or Union Territory under Article 342?
o: The Union Council of Ministers by executive order
The Parliament after consultation with the Governor
The President after consultation with the Governor
The Governor after consultation with the President
83.x: Under Article 342 the President, after consultation with the Governor, notifies the Scheduled Tribes of a State or UT (the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950). Parliament only includes or excludes communities later by law; the Governor and the Council of Ministers do not notify the list.
83.tq: Ask who performs the constitutional notification function and who is consulted.
xs: Under **Article 342**, **the President after consultation with the Governor** notifies the STs of a State/UT — option **(3)** is correct.
The first list was the **Constitution (ST) Order, 1950**; later inclusion or exclusion is made only by **Parliament by law**, not by the Governor or the Council of Ministers.
xa: ST status is **religion-neutral**; SC status is limited to **Hindu/Sikh/Buddhist** persons.
The **Lokur Committee (1965)** gave the five traits for identifying STs: **primitive traits, distinctive culture, geographical isolation, shyness of contact, backwardness**.
**705** ethnic groups are notified as STs; **Bhil** is the largest tribe and **MP** has the largest tribal population.

83.s: After the initial notification under Article 342, who alone can include a community in or exclude it from the list of Scheduled Tribes?
o: The President through a fresh notification
The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes by recommendation
83.x: Subsequent inclusion or exclusion of communities from the Scheduled Tribe list requires a law made by Parliament.
83.tq: Distinguish the original notifying authority from the authority competent to alter the list later.
xs: After the first notification, a community can be included in or excluded from the ST list only by **Parliament by law** — option **(1)** is correct.
The **President** notifies the list only once (with the Governor's consultation) under **Art. 342**; a fresh Presidential notification cannot alter it.
xa: The original list is the **Constitution (ST) Order, 1950**.
**Art. 338A** (inserted by the **89th Amendment Act, 2003**) created the **NCST**, set up in **2004** — it does not add or drop tribes.
Parliament also amends the **Fifth and Sixth Schedules** by **ordinary law**, not under **Art. 368**.

The NCST was actually set up in **2004**.
xa: NCST extra focus: **minor forest produce**, **mineral and water rights**, **rehabilitation** of displaced tribals.
**Art. 342**: President notifies STs; **Art. 244(1)**: Fifth Schedule; **Art. 244(2) and 275(1)**: Sixth Schedule.

85.s: Matters relating to the Parsi community come under which Union Ministry?
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
Ministry of Women and Child Development

n: The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment deals with transgender welfare. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 28-30]
The Ministry of Tribal Affairs deals with the Forest Rights Act. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 28-30]
The Ministry of Minority Affairs deals with Parsis. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 28-30]

85.s: Which type of public policy creates or reorganises institutions?
85.x: Constitutive policy creates or reorganises institutions; regulatory policy limits individual or firm behaviour.
xa: Distributive: **farm input subsidies, PM-KISAN**; redistributive: **land reforms, progressive income tax**.
Regulatory: **licensing**, food-safety standards; constitutive: **NITI Aayog**, **delimitation**.

85.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with its Lowi policy type?
85.x: Licensing and food-safety standards limit behaviour, so they are regulatory. Land reforms and progressive tax are redistributive; NITI Aayog is constitutive.
xa: **Distributive** examples: **farm input subsidies, PM-KISAN**.
⚠ Distributive = costs borne by all; redistributive = one group to another.

85.s: Under Lowi's classification, PM-KISAN is an example of which type of policy?
85.x: PM-KISAN is distributive: benefits go to specific groups while costs are borne by all.

85.s: Land reforms and progressive income tax are examples of which Lowi policy type?
85.x: Redistributive policies transfer from one group to another, as land reforms and progressive income tax do.

85.s: With whom is the optimal model of policy-making associated?
85.x: Dror proposed the optimal model; Easton is linked to the systems model, Bentley to group theory and Mills to elite theory.
xa: Easton's systems model: **inputs, conversion, outputs, feedback**.
**Etzioni** = mixed scanning; **Lindblom** = incrementalism.

85.s: Who propounded the 'mixed scanning' model of policy-making?
85.x: Etzioni propounded mixed scanning; Lindblom gave incrementalism and Simon bounded rationality.

85.s: With whom is the elite theory of policy-making, with the idea of the 'power elite', associated?
85.x: C. Wright Mills gave the 'power elite'; Bentley is linked with group theory and Easton with the systems model.

85.s: With whom is the group theory of public policy associated?
85.x: Group theory is linked with Arthur Bentley and David Truman.

85.s: Who gave the systems model of policy, with inputs, conversion, outputs and feedback?
85.x: David Easton gave the systems model as well as the definition 'authoritative allocation of values'.

85.s: Who gave the concepts of 'bounded rationality' and 'satisficing' in decision-making?
85.x: Herbert Simon critiqued the rational-comprehensive model with bounded rationality and satisficing.

85.s: Who described incrementalism as 'the science of muddling through' in 1959?
85.x: Charles Lindblom's 1959 essay 'The Science of Muddling Through' set out incrementalism.

85.s: Which one of the following best represents the working definition of public policy?
o: A systematic course of action adopted by the state to address public issues, achieve development goals and regulate behaviour
A judicial determination applicable only to an individual dispute
A temporary administrative order issued only during emergencies
A set of private decisions taken by market participants without state intervention
85.x: Public policy is a systematic state course of action addressing public issues, pursuing development goals and regulating behaviour; it bridges political intent and administrative action.
85.tq: Choose the precise comprehensive definition over narrower alternatives.
xs: Public policy is **a systematic course of action adopted by the state to address public issues, achieve development goals and regulate behaviour** — option **(1)** is correct.
It is the **bridge between political intent and administrative action** — not a court ruling, an emergency order or a private market decision.
xa: Simply put: **government actions, laws and rules** to address specific problems.
Indian bases: **Preamble + DPSPs**, judicial interpretation, international commitments, **NITI Aayog** agendas, Budget, Economic Survey.
**Dye**: "whatever governments choose to do or not to do".

85.s: Who defined public policy as “whatever governments choose to do or not to do”?
85.x: Thomas Dye defined public policy as whatever governments choose to do or not to do, thereby treating governmental inaction also as policy.
xs: **Thomas Dye** defined public policy as "**whatever governments choose to do or not to do**" — option **(4)** is correct.
So for Dye, **inaction is also policy**.
**Easton** = "authoritative allocation of values"; **Lasswell** = "projected programme of goals, values and practices"; **Anderson** = "purposive course of action".
xa: Dye also gave **elite theory** with **Zeigler**.
⚠ **Lasswell** = founder of "**policy sciences**"; **Dye** = "do or not to do".
**Easton** also gave the **systems model** (inputs, conversion, outputs, feedback).

85.s: Who defined public policy as the 'authoritative allocation of values for the whole society'?
85.x: Easton gave this definition; Lasswell called policy a projected programme of goals, values and practices.
xa: **Lasswell** is the founder of the "**policy sciences**".
⚠ **Easton** = both a definition and the **systems model**.
**Thomas Dye**: "whatever governments choose to do or not to do".

85.s: The Right to Food, an example of judicial interpretation as a basis of Indian public policy, has been read into which Article?

xa: Public policy bridges **political intent and administrative action**.
Setting up **NITI Aayog** is itself a **constitutive** policy (Lowi).

85.s: Who is regarded as the founder of the 'policy sciences'?
85.x: Harold Lasswell founded the policy sciences; Dye and Easton are known for their definitions.

85.s: Who defined public policy as a 'purposive course of action' by actors dealing with a problem?
85.x: James Anderson defined policy as a purposive course of action followed by actors dealing with a problem.

85.s: With whom is the concept of nudges in public policy associated?

**Pressman and Wildavsky** = "Implementation" (**1973**); **Bentley and Truman** = group theory; **Lindblom and Simon** = incrementalism/satisficing.

Information instruments: **RTI Act Sec. 4** disclosure, public campaigns.

xa: Indian instruments: **regulation**, **taxes and subsidies**, **direct provision**, **information**, **nudges**.
**Nudges** = **Thaler and Sunstein**.

**Hood's "NATO" tools**: Nodality, Authority, Treasure, Organisation.
**Nudges**: behavioural design (**Thaler and Sunstein**).

85.s: Production Linked Incentives (PLI) are an example of which policy instrument?
85.x: PLI incentives and DBT subsidy reform illustrate taxes and subsidies as an instrument.

85.s: Running schools and Primary Health Centres is an example of which policy instrument?
85.x: Schools and PHCs are direct provision by the State.

85.s: Who wrote the top-down study 'Implementation' (1973), which showed how chains of clearances derail programmes?
85.x: Pressman and Wildavsky wrote 'Implementation' (1973), the classic top-down study. Lipsky (street-level bureaucracy, 1980) and Elmore (backward mapping) belong to the bottom-up approach. Thaler and Sunstein are linked with nudges.
xs: '**Implementation**' (**1973**) was written by **Pressman and Wildavsky** — option **(3)** is correct.
It is the **top-down** classic: chains of clearances derail programmes.
**Lipsky** (street-level bureaucracy, **1980**) and **Elmore** (backward mapping) are **bottom-up**; **Thaler and Sunstein** = nudges.
xa: Top-down: policy set at the centre and carried out **faithfully**.
Bottom-up: **front-line officials** shape real outcomes.

85.s: What does the bottom-up approach to policy implementation stress?
85.x: The bottom-up approach recognises that front-line officials shape actual outcomes; central direction and faithful execution mark the top-down approach.
xa: Top-down: **Pressman and Wildavsky**, "Implementation" (**1973**) — chains of clearances derail programmes.
Bottom-up: **Lipsky** "street-level bureaucracy" (**1980**); **Elmore** "backward mapping".

85.s: With whom is the concept of 'street-level bureaucracy' associated?
85.x: Michael Lipsky developed the concept of street-level bureaucracy in 1980, referring to front-line officials who shape policy outcomes.
85.tq: Separate the proponents of related implementation concepts.
xs: "**Street-level bureaucracy**" (**1980**) is **Michael Lipsky**'s concept — option **(4)** is correct.
It is a **bottom-up** view: front-line officials shape outcomes.
xa: **Richard Elmore**: "**backward mapping**" (also bottom-up).
**Pressman and Wildavsky** (**1973**): the top-down classic.
**Simon**: satisficing; **Easton**: systems model.

85.s: With whom is 'backward mapping' in policy implementation associated?
85.x: Richard Elmore is associated with the bottom-up implementation concept of backward mapping.
85.tq: Discriminate between the two bottom-up implementation scholars.
xs: "**Backward mapping**" is **Richard Elmore**'s idea — option **(2)** is correct.
It belongs to the **bottom-up** approach, like **Lipsky**'s street-level bureaucracy.
xa: **Dror** = optimal model; **Lindblom** = incrementalism.
Top-down: **Pressman and Wildavsky** (**1973**).

Option (1) is **assimilation**; (2) is **homogenisation**; (3) is **hybridisation**.
xa: ⚠ **Acculturation** = both change, stay distinct; **Assimilation** = minority loses identity.
**Diffusion** = spread of cultural traits from one society to another.
**Glocalisation** = global products adapted to local tastes, e.g. local menus of global food chains.

104.s: What is the process called in which a minority culture is absorbed into the dominant culture and loses its distinct identity?
104.x: Assimilation occurs when a minority culture is absorbed into the dominant culture and loses its distinct identity.
104.tq: Use the identity-loss clue to distinguish assimilation from acculturation.
xs: A minority culture absorbed into the dominant one, **losing its identity**, is **assimilation** — option **(1)** is correct.
In **acculturation** both cultures change but **stay distinct** — the key trap.
**Glocalisation** is local adaptation; **hybridisation** is blending into new forms.
xa: ⚠ **Acculturation** = both change, stay distinct; **Assimilation** = minority loses identity.
**Homogenisation** = cultures converge towards one global pattern.

104.s: What is the spread of cultural traits from one society to another called?
104.x: Diffusion is the spread of cultural traits from one society to another. Assimilation is absorption into a dominant culture, homogenisation is convergence to one pattern, and glocalisation is local adaptation of global products.
104.tq: Diffusion: traits spread like ink in water.
xs: Spread of cultural traits from one society to another is **diffusion** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Assimilation** = minority absorbed; **homogenisation** = convergence to one pattern; **glocalisation** = local adaptation of global products.
xa: **Acculturation**: two cultures exchange traits, both change but stay distinct.
**Hybridisation**: global and local mix into new, blended forms.

104.s: What is the blending of global and local cultural elements called?
104.x: Hybridisation is a blend of global and local elements; glocalisation is local adaptation, homogenisation is convergence to one pattern.

104.s: Which of the following describes globalisation?
o: Liberalisation of trade in goods alone, with restrictions on capital flows
Free flow of goods, services, capital, technology, ideas and people across borders
Nationalisation of foreign enterprises to protect domestic industry
Free movement of people while restricting trade in goods and services
104.x: Globalisation means the free flow of goods, services, capital, technology, ideas and people across national borders.
104.tq: Globalisation lets everything flow: goods, money, ideas and people.
xs: **Globalisation** = **free flow of goods, services, capital, technology, ideas, people** — option **(2)** is correct.
Options (1) and (4) restrict some flows; (3) nationalisation is the opposite of globalisation.
xa: **Anthony Giddens**: globalisation as **time-space distanciation**; "runaway world".
**ES 2025-26**: shift from **"hyper-globalisation"** to **"geostrategic globalisation"**.
Criticism: widens rich-poor gaps; can become **"commercial imperialism"**.

104.s: What shift does the Economic Survey 2025-26 describe?
104.x: The Economic Survey 2025–26 describes a shift from ‘hyper-globalisation’ to ‘geostrategic globalisation’.
104.tq: Test the exact paired terminology and avoid replacing a qualified shift with an extreme one.
xs: **ES 2025-26** describes a shift from **"hyper-globalisation"** to **"geostrategic globalisation"** — option **(4)** is correct.
It does not describe complete **deglobalisation** or a return to protectionism.
xa: ES 2025-26: remittances and services exports keep the **CAD** stable despite the **trade deficit**.
Globalisation = free flow of goods, services, capital, technology, ideas, people.

104.s: Which of the following best captures a major criticism of globalisation?
o: It narrows all income differences between countries
It prevents the movement of capital and labour across borders
It widens gaps between rich and poor and may become a form of commercial imperialism
It affects only cultural life and not economic relations

Complete elimination of local cultural influences

Consider the following statements about globalisation and women:

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

xs: Only statement **2** is correct — **2 only**, option **(2)** is correct.
**1** is wrong: self-employed women have nearly **tripled**, not doubled, since **2017-18**.
**2** is correct: among rural migrants, **48%** of women vs **5.9%** of men.

**29%** of tertiary-educated youth unemployed in **2023-24**.

o: Guaranteed expansion of all domestic firms
Transfer of all unskilled labour to MNCs
Shutdowns and layoffs, with skilled labour moving to MNCs and unskilled labour left behind
End of competition between domestic firms and MNCs

104.s: Who among the following gave the concept of the 'space of flows'?

xa: **Ritzer** — McDonaldisation; **Appadurai** — five "scapes".
**Wallerstein** — **world-systems theory**: core, semi-periphery, periphery.

104.s: Which of the following is NOT one of Arjun Appadurai’s five ‘scapes’?
104.x: Appadurai’s five scapes are ethnoscapes, mediascapes, technoscapes, financescapes and ideoscapes. ‘Politiscapes’ is not included in this list.

**Arjun Appadurai**'s five scapes: **ethnoscapes, mediascapes, technoscapes, financescapes, ideoscapes**.
xa: **Castells**: **network society**, "space of flows".
**Giddens**: time-space distanciation; **"runaway world"**.

104.s: Into which parts does Immanuel Wallerstein's world-systems theory divide the global system?
o: Developed, developing and least developed regions only

Centre-hinterland or North-South-East divisions are not Wallerstein's terms.
xa: **Appadurai**: five "scapes"; **Castells**: network society.
**World Inequality Report 2026**: **Global South** transfers more than **1%** of world GDP to the **Global North** each year.

104.x: George Ritzer developed the concept of McDonaldisation of society. The five scapes belong to Arjun Appadurai, space of flows to Manuel Castells, and runaway world to Anthony Giddens.
104.tq: Check the scholar-concept pair and reject the swapped theorist names.
xs: **George Ritzer — McDonaldisation of society** is correct — option **(1)** is correct.
**Five scapes** belong to **Appadurai**; **space of flows** to **Castells**; **runaway world** to **Giddens**.
xa: **Wallerstein** = **world-systems theory**.
**Robertson** = **glocalisation**; "the world as a single place".

104.s: Who among the following gave the concepts of 'time-space distanciation' and the 'runaway world'?
104.x: Giddens gave time-space distanciation and the 'runaway world'; Castells gave the network society.

104.x: Roland Robertson is linked with glocalisation; Ritzer with McDonaldisation.

104.tq: 40 for the top 1%, 65 for the top 10%.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — **1 only**, option **(1)** is correct.
**1**: per **World Inequality Report 2026**, India's **top 1%** hold about **40%** of wealth.
**2** is wrong: the **top 10%** hold about **65%**, not 75%.
xa: The report is by the **World Inequality Lab**.
**Global South** transfers more than **1%** of world GDP to the **Global North** each year.
Official view: inequality matters less than in the early 2010s; **HCES 2023-24** comparability disputed.

104.s: According to Oxfam India's 'Survival of the Richest' (2023), the top 1% held what share of India's wealth in 2021?
104.x: Oxfam found the top 1% held 40.5% of wealth in 2021, while the bottom 50% held about 3%.

104.s: According to the World Inequality Report 2026, India's top 10% hold about what share of wealth?
104.x: The World Inequality Report 2026 puts India's top 10% at about 65% and the top 1% at about 40% of wealth.

Consider the following statements about Oxfam India's 'Survival of the Richest':
1. It was released in January 2023.

104.s: According to the World Bank's Spring 2025 Poverty and Equity Brief, what was India's consumption-based Gini index in 2022-23?
104.x: The World Bank put India's consumption-based Gini at 25.5 in 2022-23, down from 28.8 in 2011-12.

105.s: "Culture is the part created by man in the environment". Who said this ?
105.x: 'Culture is the man-made part of the environment' is M.J. Herskovits's definition (Man and His Works, 1948). Tylor defined culture as a 'complex whole' of knowledge, belief, art, morals, law and custom, and Malinowski as inherited artefacts, goods and ideas, so 'None of the above'.

105.s: Who first mentioned the concept of "social evolution" ?
105.x: Herbert Spencer was among the first to study society from an evolutionary point of view; his Social Statics (1851) already framed social evolution, and he coined 'survival of the fittest'. Comte gave the law of three stages, Lester Ward 'telesis' (printed key: Lester F. Ward).

105.s: Who said "Society is a fabric of social relations"?
105.x: MacIver and Page called society 'a web (fabric) of social relationships'. Weber is linked with social action, Veblen with the leisure class and Marx with class struggle.

105.s: "Society is like a weaving work of social relations." With whom of the following is this comment associated?
105.x: 'Society is a web of social relationships' is MacIver's definition (MacIver and Page, Society); it is not from Marx, Durkheim or Weber.

105.s: Who proposed the concept of "Social capillary" ?
105.x: 'Social capillarity' was coined by the French demographer Arsène Dumont (Dépopulation et Civilisation, 1890): the pursuit of upward mobility makes families limit births, like liquid rising in a capillary tube. Louis Dumont (Homo Hierarchicus) is the caste scholar, a trap (printed key: Louis Dumont).

105.s: What kind of authority does the tribal leader exercise ?
105.x: A tribal chief's authority rests on custom and tradition, so it is Weber's traditional authority, not rational-legal or magical power.

105.s: Which of the following is included in Weber's typology of action ?
o: Rational action with respect to purpose, rational action with respect to values, emotional action, conventional action
Conventional Action, Populist Action, Rational Action
105.x: Weber's four types of social action are instrumentally (goal) rational, value-rational, affective (emotional) and traditional (conventional).

105.s: According to Karl Marx, class membership is based on what ?
105.x: For Marx, class is fixed by one's position in the relations of production (owners vs non-owners of the means of production), not by authority or prestige (Weber).

105.s: Who among the following termed sociology as "social physics" ?
105.x: Auguste Comte first called the new science 'social physics' and later renamed it 'sociology' (1838), partly because Quetelet had used 'social physics' for statistics.

105.s: Who included India in the Asiatic Mode of Production?
105.x: Karl Marx placed India in the 'Asiatic mode of production' (writings on India 1853-58): village communities without private landed property under a despotic state. Weber wrote The Religion of India (printed key: Max Weber).

105.s: What is the habit of a person occupying a position of traditional authority based on a belief in holiness and obedience?
105.x: Authority resting on belief in the sanctity of age-old custom and obedience to its holder is Weber's traditional authority.

105.s: Who is the author of the book 'Sociology of Economic Life'?
105.x: The Sociology of Economic Life (1963) is by Neil J. Smelser.

105.s: Who described Sociology as the encyclopedic science of society?
105.x: Comte (and Spencer) saw sociology as a synthetic, encyclopaedic science of society, the queen of the sciences; Sorokin and MacIver held the specialist (formal) view.

105.s: It is said that "Religion is an intoxicant of people". Who said?
105.x: Marx called religion 'the opium of the people' (intoxicant), in his Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right (1844).

105.s: Who wrote 'Communist Manifesto'?
105.x: The Communist Manifesto (1848) was written jointly by Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels, so 'Marx and Engels' is the full answer (printed key: Marx alone).

105.s: Who said "Religion is an intoxicant for people"?
105.x: 'Religion is the opium (intoxicant) of the people' is Karl Marx's remark, not Gandhi's or Lenin's.

105.s: Who said 'Religion is a heart for the heartless'?
105.x: Marx called religion 'the sigh of the oppressed creature, the heart of a heartless world' and 'the opium of the people' (1844).

105.s: According to whom 'the existence of strong personal attachments and the fact of death, which of all human events is the most upsetting and disorganizing to man's calculations, are perhaps the main sources of religious belief'?
105.x: Malinowski's functionalist theory held that strong personal attachments and death, the most upsetting of human events, are the main sources of religious belief.

105.s: Who among the following wrote The Communist Manifesto along with Karl Marx?
105.x: The Communist Manifesto (1848) was written jointly by Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels.

105.s: Scientific socialism is attributed to
105.x: Scientific socialism is attributed to Karl Marx (with Engels), as against the earlier utopian socialism.

105.s: Which one of the following is the central theme of ‘The Communist Manifesto’ written by Marx and Engels?
105.x: The Manifesto opens: 'The history of all hitherto existing society is the history of class struggles' – class struggle is its central theme.
