Match
List I (Article of Indian Constitution) with
List II (Provisions) and select the correct answer using the codes given below the lists:
List I (Article of Indian Constitution)
A. Article 16(2)
B. Article 29(2)
C. Article 30(1)
D. Article 31(1)
List II (Provisions)
1. No person shall be deprived of his property save by the authority of law
2. No person can be discriminated against in the matter of public appointment on the ground of race, religion or caste
3. All minorities whether based on religion or language shall have the fundamental right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice
4. No citizen shall be denied admission into any educational institution maintained by the State, or receiving State aid, on grounds of religion, race, caste, language or any of them

152.s:
Consider the following statements with regard to India's Foreign Policy:

I. India's Act East Policy was originally conceived as an economic initiative but had later extended into political, strategic and cultural dimensions.

II. The 'Connect Central Asia Policy' has been taken forward with the institutionalization of the 'India-Central Asia Summit' mechanism.

III. Under the 'Security and Growth for All in the Region' (SAGAR) Policy, the DRDO initiated the Marine and Allied Interdisciplinary Training and Research Initiative (MAITRI) for the purpose of establishing long-term collaboration with countries in the East Asian region.

IV. India's Think West Policy is an outreach to the Western Industrialized nations for strengthening of relations in areas of education and defence.
Which of the above statements are valid?
152.x: I and II are valid: Act East grew from an economic to a political, strategic and cultural policy, and Connect Central Asia was institutionalised through the India-Central Asia Summit (2022). III is wrong – MAITRI is DRDO's research arm of Sagar Maitri for Indian Ocean Region countries, not East Asia; IV is wrong – Think West is about West Asia (Gulf, Iran, Israel), not Western industrialised nations.

152.x:

Statement I is wrong – Look East was articulated under P.V. Narasimha Rao (1991-92), not Deve Gowda; III is wrong – it was an economic, not a counter-terrorism, policy; IV is right. b. It is an ASEAN-Centered Forum

c. It can only be chaired by an ASEAN member

d. East Asia Summit comprises of the ten member states of the ASEAN
152.src: APPSC AEE Civil & Mechanical Engineering General Studies & M
152.x: a, b and c are correct: the 13th EAS was held in Singapore (Nov 2018), the EAS is ASEAN-centred and only an ASEAN member chairs it. d is wrong – the EAS has 18 members (10 ASEAN + 8 partners incl. India, China, USA, Russia).

152.s:
Which of the following is/are correct about East Asia Summit?

a. 13th East Asia Summit held in Singapore.

b. It is an ASEAN-Centered Forum.

c. It can only be chaired by an ASEAN Member.

d. East Asia Summit comprises the ten member states of the ASEAN.
152.src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
152.x: a, b and c are correct: 13th EAS in Singapore (2018), ASEAN-centred, chaired only by an ASEAN member. d is wrong – the EAS has 18 members, not just the ten ASEAN states; so 'all of the above' is wrong.

152.s: The second edition of India Myanmar Naval Exercise IMNEX-2019 was organised at:
152.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
152.x: IMNEX-2019, the second India-Myanmar Naval Exercise, was held at Visakhapatnam (19-22 October 2019), like the first edition in 2018.

152.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's Look East and Act East policies?
o: Look East was launched in the early 1990s under P.V. Narasimha Rao
Look East was originally economic, focused on trade, investment and AIFTA with ASEAN
Act East was later extended to political, strategic and cultural fields
Act East was launched in 2014 at a SAARC Summit
152.x: Act East was launched in 2014 at the East Asia Summit in Myanmar under PM Modi, not at a SAARC Summit.
xa: Act East added **strategic, security, cultural** aims and the wider **Indo-Pacific**.
SAARC leaders were invited to the PM's swearing-in (**May 2014**) — that is **Neighbourhood First**.
Drivers of Look East: **countering China**, **new markets**, instability in **West and Central Asia** (UPSC).

152.s: What is the main focus of India's Link West (Think West) policy?
o: Australia, New Zealand and the Pacific Islands
152.x: Link West, also called Think West, focuses on the Gulf, Iran and Israel.
xa: The **GCC** is India's **largest socio-economic partner**: over **$160 billion** trade, **10 million** diaspora.
PM Modi: **15 visits** to GCC states + **two to Israel** (**Mar 2026**).
**I2U2** = **India, Israel, UAE, USA**.

152.s: At which forum was India's Act East Policy launched in 2014?
152.x: Act East was launched at the East Asia Summit in Myanmar (2014), not at a SAARC Summit.

152.s: Under which Prime Minister was India's Look East Policy (1991-92) launched?
152.x: Look East was launched under P.V. Narasimha Rao; Act East under Narendra Modi.

152.s: As what kind of policy was the Act East Policy initially conceived?
152.x: Act East began as an economic policy and was later extended to political, strategic and cultural fields with an Indo-Pacific orientation.
xa: Act East: **2014**, **Narendra Modi**; Look East: **1991-92**, Rao.
The **North-East** is the **gateway to ASEAN**.
Exam angle: "**economic origin, strategic extension**" statement pairs.

152.s: Countering China's influence, access to new markets and instability in West and Central Asia were drivers of which policy of India?
152.x: Countering China, new markets and instability in West and Central Asia were the drivers of the Look East Policy (1991-92).

152.s: Which is the fourth C added to the Commerce, Culture and Connectivity framework of the Act East Policy?
152.x: The 4th C is Capacity building, not Climate action.

152.s: With which country is the Akhaura-Agartala railway link associated?
152.x: Akhaura-Agartala is a rail link with Bangladesh, not an ASEAN-linked project like Kaladan and the Trilateral Highway.

152.s: Under the Act East Policy, which region of India is the gateway to ASEAN?
152.x: The North-East is India's gateway to ASEAN under Act East.

152.s: In which year did India and Vietnam raise their ties to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership?
152.x: Under Act East, India-Vietnam ties became a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in 2016.

152.s: Which ASEAN country became India's strategic partner in August 2025?
152.x: India and the Philippines became strategic partners in August 2025; Malaysia's ties became a CSP in 2024.

152.s: Dustlik-2019 - a first ever joint military exercise was held between India and ___:
152.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
152.x: DUSTLIK is the India-Uzbekistan joint military exercise; its first edition was held in November 2019 at Tashkent.

152.s: What is the importance of developing Chabahar Port by India?
o: India's trade with African countries will enormously increase.
India's relations with oil-producing Arab countries will be strengthened.
India will not depend on Pakistan for access to Afghanistan and Central Asia.
Pakistan will facilitate and protect the installation of a gas pipeline between Iraq and India.
152.x: Chabahar gives India an alternative route to Afghanistan and Central Asia that bypasses Pakistan, which denies India land transit.

152.s: Through which port of Iran, India sent its consignment of wheat in October, 2017 to Afghanistan by passing the Pakistan route?
152.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
152.x: India's first wheat shipment to Afghanistan (October 2017) went through Iran's Chabahar port, bypassing Pakistan.

152.s: Where was India's Connect Central Asia policy launched in 2012?
152.x: Connect Central Asia was launched at Bishkek in 2012; Samarkand hosted the first India-Central Asia Dialogue (2019).

152.s: In 2026, what did the USA do with India's sanctions waiver for Chabahar port?
152.x: In 2026 the USA ended, not extended, India's Chabahar waiver; Chabahar gives India access to Afghanistan, Central Asia and the INSTC bypassing Pakistan.

152.s: What bilateral trade target was set when India-Uzbekistan ties were raised to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in August 2026?
152.x: The August 2026 upgrade set a $5 billion trade target by 2030, along with a uranium-supply framework.
xa: Uzbekistan hosted the first India-Central Asia Dialogue (**Samarkand, 2019**).
Other upgrades: **Vietnam** CSP **2016**; **Malaysia** CSP **2024**; **Philippines** strategic partner **Aug 2025**.

152.s: The first India-Central Asia Dialogue of foreign ministers was hosted by which country and held at which city?
152.x: Uzbekistan hosted the first India-Central Asia Dialogue at Samarkand in 2019. Afghanistan was also invited.
152.tq: Pair the host country with the city rather than confusing it with the policy-launch venue.
xs: **Uzbekistan** hosted the first India-Central Asia **Dialogue** at **Samarkand** (**2019**) — option **(3)**.
**Afghanistan** was invited (**APPSC 2019**: "Uzbekistan organised the first Dialogue" = correct).
**Bishkek** is where **Connect Central Asia** was announced (**2012**).
xa: ⚠ First Dialogue = **2019**, Samarkand (ministers); first Summit = **2022**, virtual (leaders).
Uzbekistan: **Comprehensive Strategic Partnership** (**Aug 2026**).

152.s: When and how was the first India-Central Asia Summit held?
152.x: The first India-Central Asia Summit was held virtually in January 2022.
152.tq: Combine the year with the mode of meeting to distinguish the Summit from the earlier Dialogue.
xs: The first **India-Central Asia Summit** was in January **2022**, **virtual** — option **(2)**.
**2019** was the first **Dialogue** of foreign ministers, at **Samarkand**.
xa: ⚠ Dialogue = ministers (**2019**); Summit = leaders (**2022**).
**I2U2**'s first leaders' summit was also virtual, **2022**.

152.s: On which water body is Iran's Chabahar port located?
152.x: Chabahar is on the Gulf of Oman and gives India access to Afghanistan and Central Asia avoiding Pakistan.

152.s: Besides the Central Asian states, which country was invited to the first India-Central Asia Dialogue at Samarkand in 2019?
152.x: The first India-Central Asia Dialogue of foreign ministers (Samarkand, 2019) also invited Afghanistan.

152.s: Besides India, Israel and the USA, which country is a member of the I2U2, called the 'West Asia Quad'?
152.x: I2U2 is India, Israel, UAE and USA.

152.s:
Consider the following statements about India's Link West engagement:
1. India's trade with the GCC is over $160 billion.
2. The first I2U2 leaders' summit was held virtually in 2022.
3. I2U2 is handled by MEA's Economic Diplomacy Division.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
152.x: All three are correct: GCC trade exceeds $160 billion, the first I2U2 summit was virtual (2022) and it is handled by MEA's Economic Diplomacy Division.

152.s: Which grouping is India's largest socio-economic partner in West Asia, with trade of over $160 billion?
152.x: The GCC is India's largest socio-economic partner in the region, with over $160 billion trade and about 10 million Indians.

152.s: India's Think West doctrine has widened in scope into which grouping?
152.x: Think West (Gulf, Iran, Israel) has widened into I2U2.

152.s:
Consider the following statements with respect to Information Fusion Centre (IFC) for the Indian Ocean Region (IOR) and choose the correct code given below:
a. It is established with a prime vision to strengthen maritime security in the region and beyond
b. Its prime goal is to create maritime information hub for joint satellite mission in the region
c. It has been established at Gurugram, India and is jointly administered by the Indian Navy and Indian Coast Guard.
152.src: APPSC 2018 Lecturers in Government Polytechnic Colleges (Eng
152.x: a and c are correct: the IFC-IOR at IMAC Gurugram (Dec 2018) aims at maritime security through information sharing, and IMAC is jointly administered by the Indian Navy and the Coast Guard. b is wrong – it is not a hub for a joint satellite mission.

152.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's maritime visions?
o: SAGAR stands for Security and Growth for All in the Region
SAGAR was announced in Sri Lanka in 2015
MAHASAGAR (2025) stands for Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions
SHANTI was announced on 13 July 2026 by EAM Jaishankar
152.x: SAGAR (2015) and MAHASAGAR (2025) were both announced in Mauritius, not Sri Lanka.
xa: ⚠ SAGAR and MAHASAGAR were both launched in **Mauritius**; **SHANTI** by **EAM Jaishankar**, not the PM.
SHANTI will be operationalised first in the **Bay of Bengal**.

152.s: In which sea area is SHANTI, India's normative framework for shared maritime spaces, to be operationalised first?
152.x: SHANTI is a normative framework for shared maritime spaces to be operationalised first in the Bay of Bengal.
xa: Launched **13 July 2026** by **EAM Jaishankar**.
Tied to India's **UNSC 2028-29** campaign.

152.s: Under the SAGAR doctrine, how does India project itself in the Indian Ocean Region?
o: Junior partner of an external power
152.x: SAGAR presents India as a net security provider in the Indian Ocean Region, partly in response to China's String of Pearls.
xa: SAGAR: **2015**, **Mauritius**; upgraded to **MAHASAGAR** in **2025**.
**IPOI** builds on SAGAR.
Debate: the US sinking of Iran's **IRIS Dena** (**Mar 2026**) challenges the "net security provider" claim.

152.s: In which country was SAGAR (Security and Growth for All in the Region) announced in 2015?
152.x: SAGAR was announced in Mauritius in 2015; MAHASAGAR was also announced in Mauritius (2025).

152.s: Who launched SHANTI, India's framework for shared maritime spaces, on 13 July 2026?
152.x: SHANTI was launched by EAM Jaishankar, not the PM.

152.s: In which year was SAGAR upgraded to MAHASAGAR?
152.x: MAHASAGAR came in 2025 (Mauritius); SAGAR was 2015 and SHANTI 2026.

152.s: What is the full form of SAGAR in India's maritime policy?
o: Security and Growth for All in the Region
Strategic Alliance for Growth and Regional Security
Security and Governance in the Asian Region
Shared Advancement for Growth in the Region
152.x: SAGAR, announced in Mauritius in 2015, stands for Security and Growth for All in the Region.

152.s: What is the full form of MAHASAGAR, India's upgraded maritime vision of 2025?
o: Maritime Alliance for Harmony and Security Across Global and Asian Regions
Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions
Multilateral Holistic Approach to Security and Growth in the Asian Region
Mutual Help and Security Agreement for Growth and Regional Advancement
152.x: MAHASAGAR, announced in Mauritius in 2025, means Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions.

152.s: What is the full form of SHANTI, India's framework for shared maritime spaces announced in July 2026?
o: Securing Holistic Advancement through Norms, Trust and Integrity
Security and Harmony Among Nations Through Integration
Shared Harbours and Navigation Through Indian Ocean
Strategic Harmony and Norms for Trade in the Indo-Pacific
152.x: SHANTI, announced by EAM Jaishankar on 13 July 2026, stands for Securing Holistic Advancement through Norms, Trust and Integrity.

152.s: Indian coastal surveillance radars have been installed in which of the following group of countries?
o: Sri Lanka, Maldives, Mauritius and Seychelles
Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Mauritius and Seychelles
Sri Lanka, Maldives, Bangladesh and Mauritius
152.x: The coastal radar chain covers Sri Lanka, Maldives, Mauritius and Seychelles.
152.tq: Identify the complete set by eliminating the country substituted from a neighbouring maritime grouping.
xs: India's **coastal surveillance radars** are in **Sri Lanka, Maldives, Mauritius and Seychelles** — option **(1)**.
**Bangladesh** is not in the listed radar chain.
xa: Recommendation (**Mar 2026**): strengthen it along with **IORA**.
Island projects: **Agalega** (Mauritius), **Assumption Island** (Seychelles), **Hanimaadhoo** (Maldives).

152.s: Where was the Information Fusion Centre-Indian Ocean Region (IFC-IOR) inaugurated in December 2018?
152.x: IFC-IOR was inaugurated on 22 December 2018 at IMAC, Gurugram, hosted by the Indian Navy.

152.s: With India and Sri Lanka, which country formed the Colombo Security Conclave as a trilateral in 2011?
152.x: It began as India, Sri Lanka and Maldives; Mauritius, Bangladesh and Seychelles joined later.

152.s: Which city hosted the MILAN 2026 naval exercise?
152.x: MILAN 2026 was held at Visakhapatnam, linking Andhra Pradesh to Act East and SAGAR.

152.s: Which service hosts the Information Fusion Centre-Indian Ocean Region (IFC-IOR) at Gurugram?
152.x: The IFC-IOR, inaugurated on 22 December 2018 at IMAC, Gurugram, is hosted by the Indian Navy.

152.s: The coastal radar chain, IFC-IOR and island projects are flagship initiatives of which doctrine?
152.x: SAGAR (2015) widened into MAHASAGAR and IPOI; its flagships are the radar chain, IFC-IOR and island projects.

152.s: Where was the 14th East Asia Summit of November 2019, at which PM Modi proposed the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative, held?
152.x: IPOI was proposed at the 14th EAS in Bangkok; it is an open, non-treaty initiative with seven pillars that builds on SAGAR.
xa: Pillars include **Maritime Security**, **Maritime Ecology**, **Maritime Resources**, **Disaster Risk Reduction and Management**.
**Spain** joined the IPOI in **Jan 2026**.

152.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the pillars of the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative?
152.x: The seven IPOI pillars include Maritime Security, Maritime Ecology, Maritime Resources, Capacity Building and Resource Sharing, Disaster Risk Reduction and Management, Science, Technology and Academic Cooperation, and Trade, Connectivity and Maritime Transport. Nuclear Disarmament Verification is not one of them.
152.tq: Find the unrelated sector among the formally listed seven pillars.
xs: **Nuclear Disarmament Verification** is not an IPOI pillar — option **(4)**.
The **7 pillars**: **Maritime Security**; **Maritime Ecology**; **Maritime Resources**; **Capacity Building and Resource Sharing**.
Also: **Disaster Risk Reduction and Management**; **Science, Technology and Academic Cooperation**; **Trade Connectivity and Maritime Transport**.
xa: IPOI was proposed at the **14th East Asia Summit, Bangkok** (**Nov 2019**).
IPOI is open, **non-treaty**, and builds on **SAGAR**.

152.s: When did PM Modi set out India's free, open and inclusive Indo-Pacific vision at the Shangri-La Dialogue?
152.x: Prime Minister Modi set out this vision, with ASEAN centrality, in his Shangri-La Dialogue keynote in June 2018.
xa: The **Shangri-La Dialogue** is organised by **IISS** (London), in **Singapore** since **2002**.
**2026 edition**: the US called India a "**critical anchor**".

152.s: Which body organises the Shangri-La Dialogue, held in Singapore since 2002?
152.x: The Shangri-La Dialogue is run by the London-based IISS and has been held in Singapore since 2002.
xa: PM Modi's keynote was in **June 2018**.
**2026**: US called India a "**critical anchor**"; US reverted **INDOPACOM to PACOM** (**Jun 2026**).

152.s: How many pillars does the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative (IPOI) have?
152.x: IPOI has seven pillars, from Maritime Security to Trade Connectivity and Maritime Transport.

152.s: What did the Gujral Doctrine, one of the roots of Neighbourhood First, emphasise?
152.x: The Gujral Doctrine emphasised non-reciprocity, non-interference and not allowing a country's territory to be used against a neighbour.
xa: **Neighbourhood First** began in **2014** with SAARC leaders at the swearing-in.
BIMSTEC leaders were invited in **2019**.

152.s: The leaders of which grouping were invited to the PM's swearing-in in May 2014, marking the launch of Neighbourhood First?
152.x: SAARC leaders were invited to the May 2014 swearing-in; BIMSTEC leaders were invited in 2019.
xa: Aim: **physical, digital and people-to-people connectivity** across South Asia.
Roots in the **Gujral Doctrine**: non-reciprocity, non-interference.

152.s: In 2019, the leaders of which grouping were invited to the PM's swearing-in, extending Neighbourhood First?
152.x: SAARC leaders were invited in May 2014; BIMSTEC leaders in 2019.

152.s: In which country is the Agalega airstrip and jetty project located?
152.x: Agalega is in Mauritius; Assumption Island is in Seychelles; Uthuru Thila Falhu and Hanimaadhoo are in the Maldives.
xa: **SAGAR** (**2015**) and **MAHASAGAR** (**2025**) were both launched in **Mauritius**.
Coastal radar chain: **Sri Lanka, Maldives, Mauritius, Seychelles**.

152.s: Which of the following island project-country pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
152.x: Assumption Island is in Seychelles, not Maldives; the other pairs are correct.

152.s: In which country is the Hanimaadhoo airport project located?
152.x: Hanimaadhoo airport, like the Uthuru Thila Falhu harbour, is in the Maldives.

152.s: In which country is Assumption Island, linked with an Indian project, located?
152.x: Assumption Island is in Seychelles; Agalega is in Mauritius.

153.s: India participated in a joint military drill called 'Vajra Prahar 2018' in Jaipur on 1st December 2018. Name the country with whom this joint exercise was performed.
153.src: APPSC Deputy Executive Information Engineers & Inspector of
153.x: Vajra Prahar is the India-US Special Forces exercise; the 2018 edition was held at Jaipur.

153.s: The "Tiger Triumph" exercise organised in November 2019 was a
o: joint military exercise between India and USA
joint military exercise between India and Japan
joint tiger conservation exercise between India and USA
joint tiger conservation exercise between India and Japan
153.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
153.x: Tiger Triumph (November 2019) was the first India-US tri-service amphibious military exercise – not a tiger-conservation programme.

153.s: U.S.A. and Indian forces carried out a joint 'Yudha Abhyas' in October 2009. In which State of India it was carried out?
153.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (Uttar Pradesh); it is added as option 5.
Yudh Abhyas 2009 (12-29 October) was held at Babina cantonment, which lies in Jhansi district, Uttar Pradesh, near the MP border – so none of the printed States is right (official key: Madhya Pradesh).

153.s: In which area was the Indo-US military exercise 'Yudh Abhyas 2014' held ?
153.x: Yudh Abhyas 2014 was held from 17 to 30 September 2014 at Chaubattia, Ranikhet (Uttarakhand).

153.s: ‘Red Flag’ is the name of a joint exercise between India and which one of the following countries?
153.x: Red Flag is a multinational air exercise hosted by the US Air Force, so the partner country is the USA.

153.s: Which of the following statements is correct with regard to Yudh Abhyas?
o: It is an Indian military exercise with regard to Pakistan.
It is an Indian military exercise with Oman.
It is an Indian military exercise with Bhutan.
It is an Indian military exercise with the US.
153.x: Yudh Abhyas is the India-US Army exercise; it is not held with Pakistan, Oman or Bhutan.

153.s: What was the code name given to the first ever tri-service military exercise between India and USA?
153.x: Tiger Triumph is the first India-US tri-service amphibious exercise (2019).

153.s: "Malabar Exercise-2016" is a joint Naval exercise of the following Countries
153.x: Malabar 2016 was a trilateral naval exercise of India, the USA and Japan (Australia rejoined in 2020).

153.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
153.x: Vajra Prahar involves Special Forces; Yudh Abhyas is Army, Cope India is Air Force and Tiger Triumph is tri-service amphibious.
xa: **Malabar**: **Navy** (with Japan, Australia).
**Red Flag**: **US Air Force multinational** exercise.

153.s:
Consider the following statements about India–US military exercises:
1. Yudh Abhyas is a naval exercise.
2. Tiger Triumph is a tri-service amphibious exercise.
3. Red Flag is a US Air Force multinational exercise.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
153.x: Tiger Triumph is tri-service and amphibious and Red Flag is a US Air Force multinational exercise; Yudh Abhyas is an Army exercise, so statement 1 is wrong.

153.s: Cope India is an India-US exercise of which service?
153.x: Cope India is the Air Force exercise; Malabar is naval and Yudh Abhyas is Army.

153.s: Vajra Prahar between India and the US is an exercise of which force?
153.x: Vajra Prahar is a Special Forces exercise; Yudh Abhyas is the Army exercise.

153.s: Malabar is a naval exercise of India and the USA held along with which other countries?
153.x: Malabar is a naval exercise of India and the USA with Japan and Australia.

153.s: In which State was the India-US army exercise Yudh Abhyas held in November 2022?
153.x: Yudh Abhyas of November 2022 was held in Uttarakhand.

153.s: From which country has India procured Apache AH-64E(I) helicopters?
153.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
153.x: India procured AH-64E(I) Apache attack helicopters from the USA (Boeing); the IAF inducted them in 2019.

153.s: Who is the Defence Secretary of USA, who was in India recently?
153.src: Common GS for IFS, APLIS, ATT 2012
153.x: Leon Panetta, US Secretary of Defense, visited India in June 2012. John Bryson was Commerce Secretary, Eric Holder Attorney General and Hillary Clinton Secretary of State.

153.s: In which year was LEMOA, an India-US foundational defence agreement, signed?
153.x: GSOMIA was signed in 2002, LEMOA in 2016, COMCASA in 2018 and BECA in 2020.
xa: Later steps: **INDUS-X (2023)**, **Security of Supply Arrangement (2024)**, **10-year framework (Oct 2025)**.
⚠ **2018** also gave **STA-1** status.

153.s: What does the STA-1 status, granted by the US to India in 2018, give India?
o: Licence-free access to a wide range of US military and dual-use technology
Access only to civilian nuclear technology
A veto over US defence exports to third countries
153.x: STA-1 allows faster, licence-free access to a wide range of US military and dual-use technology, comparable to NATO allies, without NATO membership.
xa: ⚠ **2018** = COMCASA + STA-1.
**Major Defense Partner** came in **2016**.

153.s:
Consider the following statements about India–US foundational agreements:
1. GSOMIA concerns the protection of shared military information.
2. BECA concerns encrypted communications data and equipment.
3. COMCASA concerns encrypted communications data and equipment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
153.x: GSOMIA protects shared military information and COMCASA covers encrypted communications; BECA (2020) concerns geospatial data, so statement 2 is wrong.

153.s: In which year did the United States designate India as a 'Major Defense Partner'?
153.x: The United States designated India as a Major Defense Partner in 2016.
153.tq: Use the middle-year distinction among the successive defence milestones.
xs: The US named India a **Major Defense Partner** in **2016** — option **(2)**.
⚠ **2016** = **LEMOA** + Major Defense Partner.

153.s: What does BECA (2020), an India-US foundational agreement, deal with?
o: Geospatial data for navigation and missile targeting
153.x: BECA covers geospatial (satellite) data; encrypted communications is COMCASA, refuelling is LEMOA and military information is GSOMIA.

153.s: Which India–US foundational agreement was the first to be signed, in 2002?
153.x: The order is GSOMIA 2002, LEMOA 2016, COMCASA 2018 and BECA 2020.

153.s: Which pair of India-US defence milestones both date from 2018?
153.x: COMCASA and STA-1 status both came in 2018; LEMOA and Major Defense Partner are 2016.

153.s: Who signed the 10-year India-US defence framework of October 2025 on behalf of India?
153.x: The 10-year defence framework of October 2025 was signed by US Defence Secretary Hegseth and Defence Minister Rajnath Singh.

153.s: ‘Pivot to Asia’ is the strategy of the foreign policy of
153.x: 'Pivot to Asia' (Rebalance, 2011) was the Obama administration's shift of US foreign-policy focus to the Asia-Pacific.

153.s: Larry Pressler is associated with -
o: Ending of U.S. sanctions on military assistance to
To strengthen cordial relations between U.S and
Criticizing the proposed Military help to Pakistan by
Announcement of candidate for Presidential elections
153.x: US Senator Larry Pressler, author of the 1985 Pressler Amendment, criticised the proposed US military help to Pakistan because of its nuclear programme.

153.s: Which development is regarded as the turning point in India-US relations?
153.x: The 2008 India-US civil nuclear deal is regarded as the turning point in the relationship.
xa: The NSG waiver **allowed civil nuclear trade**.
**AP angle**: **Kovvada** (Srikakulam) is the proposed site for US-designed **AP1000** reactors.

153.s: The 'Pivot to Asia' or 'Rebalance' policy of the United States, associated with the Obama era, was announced in which year?
153.x: The Pivot to Asia, also called the Rebalance, was announced in 2011 during the Obama era to shift greater US strategic attention towards the Asia-Pacific region.
153.tq: Use the date as the discriminator in a doctrine-year question.
xs: The **Pivot to Asia / Rebalance** came in the **Obama era**, **2011** — option **(2)**.
It shifted **USA** focus to the **Asia-Pacific** (**UPPSC 2015**).
xa: **CAATSA** (**2017**): US sanctions on buyers of **Russian arms**.
**Pressler Amendment** (**1985**): barred US aid to **Pakistan** without nuclear certification.
Quad leaders' summits began in **2021**.

153.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Pressler Amendment?
o: It barred US aid to India over its nuclear programme
It required the US President to certify that Pakistan had no nuclear device
153.x: The Pressler Amendment barred US aid to Pakistan, not India, unless the President certified Pakistan had no nuclear device; it was applied in 1990.

153.s: CAATSA (2017) of the USA mainly imposes sanctions on countries that do which of the following?
153.x: CAATSA provides for US sanctions against buyers of Russian arms; India sought a waiver over its S-400 purchase.
xa: **Hyde Act (2006)** made the nuclear deal possible under US law.
India's US-origin platforms: **P-8I, C-17, Apache, MH-60R, M777**.

153.s: How are India-US relations officially described?
153.x: India-US ties are described as a Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership.
xa: US designated India a **Major Defense Partner** in **2016**.
Mechanisms: **Strategic and Commercial Dialogue (2015)**, **2+2 (2018)**, **Quad** summits (**2021**).

153.s: India sought a CAATSA waiver from the US over its purchase of which Russian system?
153.x: CAATSA (2017) sanctions buyers of Russian arms; India sought a waiver over the S-400.

158.s:
Consider the following statements relating to the World Trade Organisations (WTO).

I. The WTO deals with the global rules of trade between nations.

II. The goal of the WTO is to help producers of goods and services, exporters and importers to conduct their business.

III. The WTO, which is a successor body of the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade, came into being following the Uruguay Round of Negotiations.

IV. The WTO distances itself in framing of rules on trade in intellectual property rights.
Which of the statements given above are correct?

158.s: The Fourth Ministerial-level meeting of the World Trade Organization was held in :
158.x: The Fourth WTO Ministerial Conference was held at Doha, Qatar, in November 2001 and launched the Doha Development Agenda; Singapore (1996) was the first, Geneva (1998) the second and Seattle (1999) the third.

158.s: Which round of GATT negotiations was the Uruguay Round (1986-1993/94), which led to the creation of the WTO?
158.x: The Uruguay Round was the eighth GATT round; it involved 123 countries and created the WTO.
xa: It produced **TRIPS**, **GATS** and the **AoA**.
⚠ **Marrakesh** = WTO agreement; **Uruguay** = round that created it; **Geneva** = HQ.
**Dunkel Draft**: **20 Oct 1991**, by **Arthur Dunkel**.

158.s: Which GATT Article permits free trade agreements as exceptions to the MFN principle, if they cover substantially all trade?
158.x: GATT Article XXIV allows FTAs as MFN exceptions provided they cover substantially all trade.

The **India-EU FTA** covers **97.5%** of EU tariff lines.
GATT survives as an **integral WTO agreement**.

158.s: The World Trade Organization was established on 1 January 1995 under which agreement?
o: General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade

**GATT** was the predecessor system; **Doha** is a later round; **Singapore** hosted **MC1** (**1996**).
xa: ⚠ **Marrakesh** = WTO agreement; **Uruguay** = round; **Geneva** = HQ.
WTO membership: **166** (Mar **2026**).
Decision-making is **one-country-one-vote**, by consensus.

**Singapore** was **MC1 (1996)**; **Geneva** hosted **MC12 (2022)**; **Abu Dhabi** hosted **MC13 (2024)**.

The **Doha Development Agenda** (**2001**) has stalled.

xa: The Ministerial Conference must meet **at least once every two years**.

The US **blocked Appellate Body appointments**, paralysing the two-tier system.

158.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Anti-dumping — Duties on goods sold below normal value
TRIPS — Minimum standards for all forms of intellectual property rights

158.s: Which two agreements are identified as the only new WTO agreements concluded in the first 30 years of the organisation?

o: TBT – Food safety, animal and plant health

158.x: The SPS Agreement covers science-based food safety and animal and plant health measures; TBT covers technical standards.

158.s: What did the Doha Declaration on TRIPS and public health affirm about TRIPS?

161.s: In which year was the NPT, which entered into force in 1970, extended indefinitely?
161.x: The NPT (signed 1968, in force 1970) was extended indefinitely in 1995.
xa: ⚠ UPSC 2015 trap: only **China** and **France** among the options were NPT nuclear-weapon states.
India calls the NPT **discriminatory ("nuclear apartheid")** and won't sign until nuclear powers accept a **time-bound disarmament plan**.
**North Korea** left the NPT in **2003**; Review Conferences are held **every 5 years**.
Criticism: the NPT lets recognised powers **modernise without disarmament deadlines**.

161.s: India's principal objection to the NPT is that it:
o: does not contain any provision on nuclear energy
is discriminatory and perpetuates nuclear apartheid
recognises India as a nuclear-weapon state without conditions
161.x: India rejects the NPT as discriminatory, describing its structure as nuclear apartheid. India also seeks a time-bound disarmament plan from the nuclear powers before signing.
161.tq: Identify the stated policy objection rather than a consequence of the treaty.
xs: India rejects the NPT as **discriminatory**, calling it **"nuclear apartheid"** — so option **(3)** is correct.
India won't sign until the nuclear powers accept a **time-bound disarmament plan**.
The NPT recognises only the **P5** as nuclear-weapon states, so it does not recognise India as one.
xa: India is also **not a signatory to the CTBT** and **did not sign the TPNW**.
⚠ India is a party to **PTBT, CWC, BWC, CCW**; not to **NPT, CTBT, TPNW**.
India is called a **"de facto responsible nuclear state"** — **NFU doctrine**, export controls, entry into **3 of 4 regimes**.
The **2008 NSG India-specific waiver** opened civil nuclear trade despite India staying outside the NPT.

161.s: India has not signed the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty (CTBT) primarily because it:
o: lacks a time-bound disarmament commitment and permits subcritical tests
does not ban any form of nuclear explosion
161.x: India objects to the CTBT because it lacks a time-bound disarmament plan and still permits subcritical tests. The CTBT bans all nuclear explosions and was adopted in 1996.
161.tq: Separate India's objection to the treaty from the treaty's stated prohibition.
xs: India has not signed the **CTBT** because it has **no time-bound disarmament** and still **allows subcritical tests** — option **(1)**.
The CTBT (**1996**) **bans all nuclear explosions**, so option (3) is wrong; it is a nuclear, not chemical, treaty.
It says nothing about recognising nuclear-weapon states — that is the **NPT**, which recognises the **P5**.
xa: The CTBT is **not in force**.
The **PTBT (1963)** bans tests **except underground**; **India is a party** to it.
India **did not sign the TPNW** (in force **2021**) — it "adds nothing to customary law".
⚠ India is not a party to **NPT, CTBT, TPNW**.

161.s: In which year did North Korea withdraw from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT)?
161.x: North Korea left the NPT in 2003.
161.tq: Recall the specific withdrawal year rather than a nearby nuclear-crisis date.
xs: **North Korea** left the **NPT** in **2003** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The NPT was signed in **1968**, came into force in **1970** and was extended indefinitely in **1995**.
xa: The NPT recognises only the **P5 — US, Russia, UK, France, China** as nuclear-weapon states.
**NPT Review Conferences** are held **every 5 years**; the consensus rule lets a single state block outcomes.
**North Korea** is also outside the **MTCR**.
**Iran's Parliament** weighed an **NPT exit** in **Mar 2026** after US-Israel strikes on its nuclear sites (**June 2025**).

161.s: The NPT recognises as Nuclear Weapon States those that developed and tested a nuclear device before which date?
161.x: NPT NWS are the states that tested before 1 January 1967: US, Russia, UK, France and China.

161.x: NPT Review Conferences are held every five years, and the consensus rule lets single states block outcomes.

161.x: The CTBT was adopted in 1996 and bans all nuclear explosions, but it is not yet in force.
